strengths.t: Beginner-friendly fit: sits easier in hand than bulkier drivers, so newer arms can make it work.
Premium blends in wind: champion, Halo, Duo and glow runs stay steady into headwinds.
Controlled distance: carries a smooth S-curve that flexes back without dumping early.

catches.t: Short-lived base plastic: dX and Pro beat in to a roller fast; GStar starts flippy.

tip.label: Player tip
tip.t: Champion and Halo start beefy and beat in to a reliable max-distance slot.

catches.t: Stiff out of the box: fresh 175 g Star and Halo copies fight hard left and take effort to turn.

alt.t: Want more turn? The MVP Wave is rated more understable: 11/5/-2/2.

strengths.t: Effortless distance: pops up from hyzer and carries deep with a gentle finish.
Controllable lines: flies straight off a hyzer or holds a gentle turnover.
Sidearm bomber: neutron and beat-in Fission runs serve as max-distance forehand drivers.

catches.t: Varies by run: stability swings by plastic: glow and Eclipse 2.0 hold, Fission can roll.

tip.label: Player tip
tip.t: Heavier 170-175 g Neutron held up better than light Fission in wind.

catches.t: Gets pushed around: headwinds knock it off line, and light copies roll at full power.

alt.t: Into a headwind? Switch to the MVP Photon: 11/5/-1/2.5.

catches.t: Finicky to throw: needs a precise nose angle to reach max distance.

strengths.t: Clean flip-up flights: pops up flat from hyzer and holds a long straight line.
Slow-arm friendly: a compact 9-speed rim unlocks turnovers and carry without big power.
Sidearm friendly: flat top and low profile make it a full-flight forehand bomber.

catches.t: Blend matters: splits opinion: Proton and soft runs turn a lot; glow Eclipse flies far steadier.
Flips under power: runs flippier than a Trail; cranked throws and hard forehands turn over.

alt.t: Want a steadier 9-speed? The MVP Tesla is rated 9/5/-1/2.

strengths.t: Tunnel precision: holds straight lines with a mild finish through tight woods.
Effortless reach: flips up and pushes surprisingly far without big power.
Pick your blend: fission turns easiest; Proton and Eclipse finish firmer.

catches.t: Batch to batch: runs range from Firebird-stable to flippy, by plastic and weight.
Heavy runs resist: heavier or stiffer copies can feel too overstable to click.
Light runs flip: copies around 155 g turn over and roll, even off a hyzer.

tip.label: Player tip
tip.t: Go heavier: a 175 g Plasma copy flew the straight line expected.

alt.t: Need less flip? The Innova TeeBird is rated 7/5/0/2.

strengths.t: Wind fighter: ignores headwinds and fades hard left every time.
Sidearm control: takes full forehand torque and finishes with a flare skip.
Usable distance: the right run can push 300-400 ft before fading.

catches.t: Can be a brick: can dump early with extreme fade; Halo, flat Champion and FAF most.

alt.t: Want less fade? The MVP Volt is rated 8/5/-0.5/2.

catches.t: Run-to-run swings: dX and some Star copies fly closer to a TeeBird and can turn.

strengths.t: Built for developing arms: pops up from hyzer and glides far with modest power.
Pinpoint placement: goes where it's pointed, from straight tunnels to wide S-curves.
Sidearm shaper: halo and Champion copies give reliable forehand flip-ups and flexes.

catches.t: Inconsistent runs: stability varies wildly by plastic: Champion and Halo fly steadier than DX.
Too much for big arms: full power flips it into a roller; DX and Pro roll easiest.

alt.t: Want less turn? The Innova TeeBird is rated 7/5/0/2.

catches.t: Wind sends it right: gusts and open fields push it into a harder turn.

strengths.t: Woods versatility: faster arms hyzer-flip it through tight gaps or turn it over.
Friendly fairway: flies very straight with a mild finish, even for slower arms.
Sidearm friendly: clean releases make controlled flicks easy.

catches.t: Run-to-run variation: copies differ by plastic and weight: heavy glow holds, light Star flips.
Gets flippier with use: seasons to a late turn on flat releases within weeks.
Mixed for newcomers: splits opinion for newer arms: can turn and tank or feel short and stiff.

strengths.t: Fairway laser: holds flat lines dead straight before a dependable mild fade.
Sidearm staple: champion copies become a go-to forehand driver and expose release flaws.
Usable reach: shapes controllable hyzer, flat and flex lines to about 350 ft.

catches.t: Blend matters: stability swings by plastic, with Star often far flippier than Champion.
Stiff for beginners: can feel too overstable for newer arms until power improves.
Seasons into flippy: can grow hard to control as it beats in over the years.

strengths.t: Effortless flip-ups: rises from steep release angles and holds long sweeping turnover lines.
Slow-arm bomber: unlocks easy 300 ft carry without tournament power.
Ground-game option: bigger arms get dependable rollers and tailwind bombs.

catches.t: Flips under power: faster arms turn it over hard, even on forehands.

alt.t: Need it to hold? The Innova TeeBird3 is rated 8/4/0/2.

catches.t: Hit-or-miss copies: runs differ in stability: some show no turn while others flip fast.
Forehand learning curve: clean flicks take fieldwork to dial in.

strengths.t: Holds any line: stays locked on its release angle without drifting or dumping.
Tunnel precision: flies dead straight with almost zero fade through tight gaps.
Form teacher: shows every release mistake, which builds better habits.

catches.t: Copies vary: mako3s fly differently by run and plastic; Champion beats in fastest.
Can drift past straight: splits opinion: some copies lean right and turn over off flat throws.
No fade to save you: without a dependable finish, bad angles stay bad.

strengths.t: Two discs in one: jawbreaker and Flex runs beat in to straight, reliable lines.
Built for wind: z and ESP runs shrug off headwinds and hard torque.
Forehand friendly: flat top and shallow rim give clean, wobble-free sidearm releases.

catches.t: Softer blends age fast: jawbreaker and Cryztal lose their fade as they beat in.

tip.label: Player tip
tip.t: Keep a premium Z or ESP copy for stability and a seasoned one for straight shots.

catches.t: Not a first disc: flies definitely overstable, with hard, skipping finishes.
Love-or-hate rim: splits opinion: the shallow depth eases griplock or feels thin.

strengths.t: Hyzer-flip machine: stands up flat and drifts gently right through wooded gaps.
Effortless reach: carries tons of glide and extra distance for its speed.
Forehand touch: flips to an extremely straight flight on soft flicks.

catches.t: Too flippy for big arms: can turn all the way over and bail right when powered.

alt.t: Want it to hold? The Axiom Hex is rated 5/5/-1/1.

catches.t: Little finish: lacks a late cut back, so it won't hook around corners.
Hard to stop: can glide well past the target into trouble.

strengths.t: Dependable finish: holds straight before a smooth forward hook.
Steadier than a Hex: takes full-power and headwind throws without flipping.
Sneaky distance: carries close to fairway-driver range, Fission most.

catches.t: Beefy special plastics: glow and Eclipse runs can fly much more overstable, near a Zone.

alt.t: Want less fade? The Axiom Hex is rated 5/5/-1/1.

catches.t: Slow to season: neutron and Eclipse stay chunky for months before settling.

strengths.t: Wind beater: pushes straight into headwinds before a hard hook.
Forehand workhorse: resists hard sidearm torque and never turns into the turf.
Workable overstability: sits between a Zone and a beefy 9-speed without being too much.

catches.t: Not a first disc: can fly too overstable and dump fast, max-weight Neutron most.

alt.t: Want a softer finish? The MVP Reactor is rated 5/5/-0.5/1.5.

catches.t: Plastic changes it: runs differ by blend: Plasma beefiest, Fission and soft Proton straighter.
Middle slot squeeze: splits opinion: can feel too mild next to beefier mids.

strengths.t: Beginner-friendly laser: gives a true straight flight out of the box with a mild finish.
Woods line-shaper: carves easy hyzer flips and long sweeping turnovers through trees.
Short sidearm touch: a flat, comfortable rim releases cleanly on flicks with little ground play.

catches.t: Leaks under power: flat or overpowered throws drift right and keep going.

alt.t: Want less turn? The Discraft Buzzz is rated 5/4/-1/1.

catches.t: Seasons flippy: can turn more as it wears, drifting past a Mako3 feel.
Run differences: fLX and Tour runs turn more out of the box than domey Z.

strengths.t: Instant utility shots: tips onto its edge for long ground rollers with little arm speed.
Air-shot versatility: steep hyzers stand up into sweeping turnover glides.
Scramble specialist: opens up unusual lines and awkward recovery shots.

catches.t: Hard to keep airborne: flat or full-power throws roll right away, often as cut rolls.

alt.t: Need it to stay up? The MVP Detour is rated 5/5/-2/1.

catches.t: Base plastic rolls sooner: star and DX turn over quicker than Halo or glow runs.
Demands finesse: needs smooth, torque-free release or it drops out.

strengths.t: Driving putter: absorbs full-power throws and flies straight before a dependable fade.
Sneaky reach: flies farther than most putters, out to 350 ft.
Calm in breezes: holds flat through moderate wind and crosswinds.

catches.t: Blend changes everything: stability swings by plastic: Electron flips, Eclipse is beefy.
Seasons quickly: fresh copies beat in fast to straighter flights.
Weak in the circle: longer putts fade early and fall short; Neutron gets slippery wet.

strengths.t: Laser-like touch: flies dead straight with gentle glide off the tee and on upshots.
Circle confidence: shallow beadless rim gives clean, floaty putts that hold chains.
Surprising reach: hyzer flips can carry 300 ft and beyond.

catches.t: Flips under power: turns over when thrown hard or released poorly.

alt.t: Need more fade? The Axiom Envy is rated 3/3/0/2.

catches.t: Edge discomfort: the beadless rim can feel sharp or grab fingers.

strengths.t: Driving putter staple: takes full power without flipping and settles with a mild fade.
Circle grabber: soft blends grab chains and die on contact.
Sneaky reach: goes unreal long for a putter, near 400 ft.

catches.t: Fragile in breezes: low-power throws can flip or drop out in wind.
Polarizing bead: splits opinion: the pronounced rim ridge feels great or gross.
Unreliable runs: copies can fly inconsistently, warped ones most.

strengths.t: Wind cutter: fights headwinds and torque with a hard, fading finish.
Sidearm approach: beadless rim releases cleanly on flicks and fights out of anhyzers.
Built to last: 500 Spectrum stays overstable for years.

catches.t: Not a first disc: dumps hard and short, so 200 ft takes real effort.

alt.t: Want more carry? The Axiom Envy is rated 3/3/0/2.

catches.t: Runs away on landing: hard ground brings big flare skips past the pin.

strengths.t: Wind and utility: champion, Metal Flake and Halo runs fight headwinds with a hard hook.
Sidearm bomber: serves as a max-distance flex driver off the forehand, best once beat in.
Repeatable flight: lands in a tight spread throw after throw, out to about 450 ft.

catches.t: Beefy out of the box: fresh, max-weight and Metal Flake runs can hook hard left early.

tip.label: Player tip
tip.t: Lighter GStar or beat-in Star runs turn more and suit intermediate arms.

catches.t: Run-to-run swings: splits opinion: copies range from flippy to beefy, even in one plastic.
Not a first disc: slower arms get instant spike hyzers and short drives.

alt.t: Slower arm? The Innova Wraith is a speed lower and known for distance: 11/5/-1/3.

strengths.t: Fairway precision: neutron and Proton hold straight lines through tight woods.
Easy distance: often the longest disc in the bag, with less effort than wide rims.
Sidearm ready: takes hard forehands without rolling over.

catches.t: Run lottery: copies range from overstable to wildly flippy, even within Neutron.

alt.t: Want consistency? The MVP Tesla is known for a reliable fade and accuracy: 9/5/-1/2.

catches.t: Flips at speed: light, Fission and some fresh copies turn over and can roll.

tip.label: Player tip
tip.t: Go 165-175 g: the heavier copies held straighter lines.

catches.t: Wear changes it: use moves it from stable to straight, then to a roller.

strengths.t: Slow-arm distance: massive turn and glide carry developing throwers much farther.
Shot-shaping tool: steep hyzers pop up flat and glide a long way; anhyzers become rollers.
Premium-plastic control: halo Star holds lines without turning and burning.

catches.t: Big arms overpower it: flat, powered throws flip hard and burn, worst in GStar or Champion.

alt.t: Big arm? The Innova Wraith holds a flex line and is known for distance: 11/5/-1/3.

catches.t: Numbers mislead: splits opinion: copies can fly far more stable than -5 turn, Halo especially.
Learning curve: each copy flies a little differently, so it takes time to figure out.

strengths.t: Effortless carry: massive glide keeps low-power throws aloft with a soft finish.
Tight-line tool: flips to flat and holds anhyzer and tunnel lines through woods.
Beginner friendly: easy, straight hyzer flips suit newer and senior throwers.

catches.t: Big arms flip it: power or a headwind can turn it over and burn.

alt.t: Big arm? The Innova TeeBird is known for a reliable fade and accuracy: 7/5/0/2.

catches.t: Beats in fast: wear makes it flippy within months, fastest in Retro plastic.
Plastics differ: opto Orbit and Gold Ice fly stiffer than Gold Line; max-weight is straighter.

strengths.t: Power-proof control: pushes straight at speed, then finishes with a dependable fade.
Sidearm workhorse: halo and Champion hold long flex lines off the forehand.
Into the breeze: flat, stiff GStar and Champion punch through headwinds.

catches.t: Plastic matters: splits opinion: Halo copies can fly far beefier than Star or color-glow runs.
Not a first disc: champion and Halo copies drop hard for slower arms until beaten in.

alt.t: New thrower? The Innova TeeBird is known for a reliable fade and accuracy: 7/5/0/2.

catches.t: Loses its finish: star copies wear toward understable, while Halo holds up for a year.

strengths.t: Classic control: holds straight through tree lines, then fades reliably at the end.
Ages well: one copy can be thrown through its whole life, from beefy to Leopard-like.
Weather ready: champion and heavy copies push through headwinds and stay true.

catches.t: Stiff for slow arms: new Champion and some Star copies fly too overstable for modest power.

alt.t: Slower arm? The Latitude 64 River is known for glide and easy starts: 7/7/-1/1.

catches.t: Copy lottery: copies range from Leopard-like to Firebird-like off the shelf.
Can lose its fade: worn Pro and some Star copies can turn over, even in a light headwind.

strengths.t: Dependable finish: thrown hard, it won't turn over and fades left on time.
Wind fighter: vIP and Tournament runs fly through strong headwinds as if calm.
Forehand trust: clean sidearm releases give a reliable left finish on upshots.

catches.t: Loses its bite: bT plastics straighten as they season, while VIP holds its fade.

tip.label: Player tip
tip.t: Pick VIP, or cycle BT copies, to keep the overstable finish.

catches.t: Less fade than rated: domey and some premium copies fly straighter than a 0/3.

alt.t: Want a harder finish? The Innova Pig glides less and is known for accuracy: 4/1/0/3.

catches.t: Grip complaints: the deep beaded rim can catch fingers and add flutter.

strengths.t: Pinpoint control: holds dead-straight lines with a soft finish, even in gusts.
Long for a mid: glides close to fairway-driver distance.
Hand feel: grippy plastic and a slim rim release cleanly on touch shots.

catches.t: Plastic changes it: splits opinion: Fission flies neutral while Eclipse can run quite overstable.
Overpowered flips: hard throws into headwind can turn it over, and wind pushes it around.

alt.t: Windy rounds? The MVP Reactor is known for a reliable fade and forehands: 5/5/-0.5/1.5.

catches.t: Can hook late: glide magnifies the fade when thrown high.

strengths.t: Benchmark control: holds straight lines with a gentle checkup across every plastic.
Forehand comfort: flat top feels steady on sidearm upshots from awkward spots.
Good learning disc: predictable flight shows mistakes while still rewarding newer throwers.

catches.t: Fades when fresh: new copies fade more than a Mako3 below full power.

alt.t: Want zero fade? The Innova Mako3 is known for accuracy and holding lines: 5/5/0/0.

catches.t: Wear changes it: use can strip its finishing fade within months.
Plastics differ: cryztal, newer and some ESP runs fly beefier than classic Z.

strengths.t: Shot-shaping tool: pops up from hyzer and holds sweeping turnover lines through woods.
Beginner friendly: gentle turn and big glide give slower arms easy distance.
Steadier options: heavier VIP and Orbit plastic resist burning for precise hyzer flips.

catches.t: Flips with power: hard throws burn it into the dirt; it rewards low effort.

alt.t: Bigger arm? The Axiom Hex turns less and is known for accuracy: 5/5/-1/1.

catches.t: Beats in fast: tree hits and wear make it unreliably flippy quite quickly.
Batch differences: newer domey runs fly more stable than old flat-top copies.

strengths.t: Torque-proof finish: fights out of turn and dumps right by the target, even off forced anhyzers.
Sidearm go-to: handles wobbly and power forehands on approaches.
Wind fighter: low glide won't sail past in headwinds.

catches.t: Not a first disc: near-zero glide finds the ground fast and can leave shots short.

alt.t: Want more carry? The Westside Harp glides more and is known for a reliable fade: 4/3/0/3.

catches.t: Mixed comfort: r-Pro can feel thin and Luster too deep to power-grip; the shape can feel clunky.
Bag overlap: splits opinion: it fills the same role as a Zone, so pick one.

strengths.t: Utility workhorse: fights out of any forced anhyzer and dumps with a big skip.
Sidearm muscle: handles full-power forehands and sharp doglegs.
Built for storms: drops straight out of the sky in heavy wind.

catches.t: Not a first disc: so overstable it can't be made to fly flat or hold a long line.

alt.t: Want less dump? The Axiom Pyro is known for overstability and forehands: 5/4/0/2.5.

catches.t: Slow to beat in: proton copies barely season and stay beefy for years.
Limited carry: almost no glide drops it like a rock, shortening shots.

strengths.t: Shot-shaping tool: steep hyzers pop to flat and drift through tight gaps.
Touch-shot ally: turns and carries straight at low power for slow arms.
No-flick solution: gives forehand-style lines off a backhand for players without one.

catches.t: Big arms overpower it: flat or ripped throws turn straight into a roller.

alt.t: Want a little fade? The MVP Detour is known for holding lines and accuracy: 5/5/-2/1.

catches.t: Finicky control: short shots and forehands need careful touch; hyzer flips can go too far.
Niche bag slot: rarely earns an everyday spot, despite doing shots nothing else does.

strengths.t: Distance control: runs out of air and drops without skipping past.
Angle control: takes power without turning over, holding the release line.
Sidearm favourite: concave top locks in for soft forehand approaches.

catches.t: No glide: it demands a hard throw to reach even short targets.

alt.t: Want some float? The Streamline Pilot is known for lots of glide and accuracy: 2/5/0/1.

catches.t: Tricky to putt: can be hard to sink from beyond close range.
Changes with wear: k3 and old K1 Soft lose late stability as they beat in.

tip.label: Player tip
tip.t: Premium K1 holds its torque resistance longest.

strengths.t: Point-and-shoot control: flies dead straight with a gentle late fade on approaches.
Easy reach: glide carries it as far as most midranges with little effort.
Hand feel: flat top and micro-bead sit naturally for forehands and backhands.

catches.t: Run lottery: plastic choice swings it from overstable to flippy; Eclipse splits opinion.
Durability concerns: baseline Electron can chunk or warp; worn copies lose stability.

tip.label: Player tip
tip.t: Eclipse stays stable even when beaten up.

catches.t: Flips if forced: yanked throws can turn and burn, like a flippier Proxy.

alt.t: Want more fade? The Axiom Envy is known for a reliable fade and accuracy: 3/3/0/2.

strengths.t: Point-and-shoot accuracy: holds any release angle to the ground with almost no fade.
Hand feel: beadless, low rim releases cleanly with a tacky grip.
Two-in-one utility: putts true with spin or push and still drives well.

catches.t: Batch lottery: stability varies by run and plastic, from Envy-stable to flippy glow.
Escapes when ripped: snapped or flat full-power throws can turn over; it's no hyzer disc.

alt.t: Want a fade to finish? The Axiom Envy is known for a reliable fade and accuracy: 3/3/0/2.

strengths.t: Torque-proof finish: fights out of forced anhyzers and dumps hard on every throw.
Forehand favourite: handles hard sidearm flicks and flex shots cleanly.
Hand feel: k1 and K1 Soft grip well and absorb landings.

catches.t: Plastic swings: k1 and K3 fly like different discs; K3 is shorter with little glide.
Unusual shape: splits opinion: the deep rim and dome take time to get used to.
Not a first disc: little glide and a hard dump suit players who already control approaches.

alt.t: Newer arm? The Axiom Envy fades less and is known for accuracy: 3/3/0/2.

strengths.t: Shot-shaping putter: flips up and holds slow right-turning lines through woods.
Pleasant in hand: shallow, rounded lip feels comfortable and grippy.
Beginner friendly: easy flip-ups and floating glide suit newer and slower arms.

catches.t: Hard to rip: flat, fast throws turn it nearly into a roller.

alt.t: Want less turn? The Latitude 64 Pure holds lines and is known for accuracy: 3/3/-1/1.

catches.t: Specialty slot: can be a niche disc used only a couple of times a round.
Plastic changes it: 750 runs fly beefy, while 300 drifts right the most.
